alignments.note: Rule 45: preposition plus governed demonstrative rendered by one English word answering to neither token separately; headed on the governed word and on 'Therefore'.
Accusative subject of the infinitive, expressed in Greek and realized by 'we'.
Support-verb rendering 'give heed'; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement, the infinitival 'to' riding along under rule 7. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Comparative adverb rendered by the whole 'the more earnest'; headed on 'more', which realizes the comparative.
Rule 32: substantival article before a participle keeps only the nominal expression; rule 22 heads on the nominal word 'things', the case preposition riding along under rule 21.
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; relativizer and copula are helpers on the participle under rules 7 and 9.
Single conjunction token rendered by the two-word clause-introducer 'lest haply', headed on 'lest'.

Subject and the English verb's required complement 'from them' ride with the verb that licenses them under rule 7; rule 103's resumptive-pronoun contrast points the same way. Marking 'from* them*' 'added' remains defensible, since its antecedent is already spent on s007/s008.

review_notes: Rule 45 chosen over an ordinary split for 'Dia touto': the ASV writes a single word 'Therefore' answering to neither token separately, unlike 'For this cause'.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause is not in question for 'the more earnest heed'; the supplied 'the' belongs with the comparative adverb it determines.
